text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R6", "statement": "Corrected finding: notifications/sms.py has no send_sms(phone, text) function and messages are not free text. Texts are queued with queue_sms(household_id: str, template_id: str, params: dict, *, now=None) -> SmsMessage, which requires the household to exist (get_household) and have household.sms_ok True, then renders an approved template from the TEMPLATES dict via render(template_id, params) -> str. render() raises KeyError for a template_id not in TEMPLATES and raises ValueError if the rendered text exceeds MAX_LENGTH = 140 characters (not 160). queue_sms() appends the SmsMessage (fields: id, household_id, phone, template_id, params, text, queued_at) to outbox/sms.jsonl via store.append_jsonl, assigning a new id with format_sms_id(next_number(..., 'SMS-')). A resend script must therefore re-queue each failed message using its original template_id and params (not arbitrary text), and can identify failed messages via delivery_status() -> dict[str, str], which reads data/sms_status.json (e.g. {\"SMS-00001\": \"delivered\", \"SMS-00002\": \"failed\"}); messages with no entry are new/unsent. Note queue_sms() raises RuntimeError if feature('sms_enabled') is false, and the outbox is irreversible: nothing ever removes or edits a line in outbox/sms.jsonl.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}]}}
